title: diff_scenarios for a pipe-replacement plan

blocks.text: A gas utility plans its pipe replacements by quarter, and its planning tool keeps each scenario as a record: a name and a plan, the list of funded replacements, each with an `id` and a `start` such as `"2028-Q3"`. Every time a scenario is re-run, the program managers ask the same thing: what changed since the last one? Write the function the tool will call for it, `diff_scenarios(a, b)` in `gas_plan.py`, comparing scenario `a`'s plan with scenario `b`'s. It returns a dictionary:

items: `"adds"`: the ids in `b`'s plan and not in `a`'s, sorted;
`"drops"`: the ids in `a`'s plan and not in `b`'s, sorted;

`"shifts"`: one entry per id in both plans with a different start, sorted by id, each a dictionary `{"id", "from", "to", "quarters"}` where `quarters` is how many quarters later `b` starts it than `a` does (negative when earlier).

blocks.text: Plans list their rows in any order. Write `quarters(start)` first, a count of quarters that makes the difference of two starts the number of quarters between them, and say how $`(y, q)`$ maps to one integer. Then state the three lists as set expressions over $`P_a`$ and $`P_b`$, the ids of the two plans, and $`a(i)`$, $`b(i)`$, their starts. The tests use their own pipes.

cases.says: adds and drops are found by project id, whatever order the plans list their rows in
a project in both plans with the same start is not reported as a shift
a move from the last quarter of one year to the first of the next is one quarter
a move to an earlier quarter is a negative shift

origin.section: A Plan Diff Needs the Input Diff and the Money Beside It

concepts: two plans are compared by project id into selected, deferred and shifted lists
a shift records both start years, so it can be read as earlier or later
